predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: Anjou and Maine: Robert the Strong's county and mission in 861

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: nearly all the land between the Loire and the Seine, excluding Anjou and the territory ceded to the Normans in 911

ledger.x: 861: Charles the Bald makes peace with Robert the Strong and appoints him Count of Anjou and margrave of Neustria, re-creating the Breton March.
863: By the Treaty of Entrammes Charles the Bald recognises western Anjou as part of Brittany under Salomon.
886: Charles the Fat gives Odo the title of margrave; the March page names no land.
936: The title dux Francorum is revived for Hugh the Great, 'Between 936 and 943'; in 943 the king 'invested Hugh with the duchy of France' (Flodoard).

936: Hugh the Great holds 'nearly all the land between the Loire and the Seine, excluding Anjou'; the page does not say when Anjou left Robertian hands, so the loss is booked at the first year the page excludes it (confidence 1).
946: Hugh the Great releases the captured Louis IV on condition that he surrender Laon.
953: Hugh makes peace with Louis IV, the Church and Otto the Great; the page does not say Laon went back, but Laon is not Robertian by Lothair's reign (confidence 1).
960: Lothair makes Hugh Capet a duke and adds Poitou to the land his father held.
987: Hugh Capet becomes King of the Franks and the duchy merges into the crown: 'The title fell into abeyance after Hugh succeeded to the French throne in 987.'

wars.name: Robert the Strong's war against Salomon and the Vikings
wars.outcome: Robert hired the former Seine Vikings against Salomon in 862 ('6,000 pounds silver'); Salomon made his peace in 863 and western Anjou was recognised as Breton; Robert was killed at Brissarthe on 2 July 866 by Vikings under Hastein and Bretons under Salomon.

wars.name: Hugh the Great and Louis IV
wars.outcome: Louis IV attacked Hugh's fortresses from 938; Louis was captured by the Normans and handed to Hugh in 945; Hugh freed him in 946 on condition he surrender Laon; Hugh was excommunicated at Ingelheim in 948 and made peace with Louis, the Church and Otto the…

certainty.note: A march and a ducal title, never a bounded state: the pages give 'the region between the Loire and the Seine' and a few counties; every frontier is approximate.
